headline: Keep {arm:September}: both candidates cost {cost.uplift_range} more per reply, and neither keeps Kairo in character better.
lede: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is clearly worse in character, down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points, and {arm:1017} is no better; both still stay within the {aspect.margin|int}-point margin the question allows. Only a candidate cheaper than {arm:September} could change the answer, which an earlier round claimed for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and this run contradicts.

caveats.material_if: Only for whether {arm:1017}'s character loss belongs to the model: it spends {reasoning_ratio.1017|pct} of its output reasoning against {arm:September}'s {reasoning_ratio.September|pct}. Its higher cost is measured at the share it ran.

decision.text: Keep {arm:September} in production. At {scoreboard.September.reply_cost_usd|usd_per_1k} it is the cheapest option measured. Both candidates stay within the question's margin, but neither keeps Kairo in character better.

{arm:qwen3.8-flash}: clearly worse in character, by {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points (within the margin), and it costs {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} more.

{arm:1017}: costs {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} more for no gain. Its pass rate is not separated from {arm:September}'s, and on holding character alone it is clearly lower.

An earlier round found {arm:qwen3.8-flash} cheaper than production; this run finds it dearer. Its production cost was recorded on {measure.production_replicating_cost.qwen3.8-flash.n|int} of its {scoreboard.qwen3.8-flash.usable|int} usable trials.

{arm:September} is weak in off-lane asks too, in character on {strata.off_lane.September.persona.holds_character.mean|pct} of them, the weakest stratum large enough to read; any future candidate will be read there.
Reconcile {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s cost with the earlier round before running it again: only a cheaper candidate could reopen this call.

claims.text: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} keeps Kairo in character clearly less often than {arm:September}, down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points, though within the margin; {arm:1017} is not separated from it.

evidence.caption: Change in pass rate against {arm:September}, the control, with {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} intervals. The shaded band is the {aspect.margin|int}-point margin, set after the results; both candidates sit inside it, and the call is the same at any margin.

claims.text: Both candidates cost more per reply than {arm:September}, by {cost.uplift_range}, and both differences stay clear of zero after correction.

evidence.caption: Corrected contrasts against {arm:September} at {family.level}, the level that holds across all {family.family_size|int} comparisons together.

claims.text: Off-lane asks, the largest stratum, carry about {strata.off_lane.loss_share.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character|pct10} of {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s character loss and about {strata.off_lane.loss_share.1017.persona.holds_character|pct10} of {arm:1017}'s.

evidence.caption: Change in holding character against {arm:September} in the largest strata, uncorrected: leads, not findings.

claims.text: Each model's frozen off-lane failure slips differently: {arm:September} answers like a help desk, {arm:qwen3.8-flash} helps with a landlord email, and {arm:1017} queues a voice line that reads as a backstage recap.

evidence.caption: The only failed off-lane trial frozen for each arm, so these show kinds of slip, not how common each is. Excerpts show the end of each transcript, often music-search output; the judge's reason names the failing line.

method.text: {cases|int} replayed cases, each run {repeats|int} times on every arm. Intervals are over cases, not attempts.

The campaign does not state what makes a trial pass; the pass rate is the share of usable trials its grader marked passed. For every arm it is lower than the rate of holding character, so pass is the stricter test. {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s drop holds on holding character alone too, so the lead finding does not rest on the undefined measure.
Readings against the control are at {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level}. Contrasts are corrected together by Holm's method at {family.level}, across {family.family_size|int} comparisons.

The margin lets a candidate's pass rate be up to {aspect.margin|int} points worse. Its floor reads the pass rate for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} but holding character for {arm:1017}; the two are shown separately and neither changes the call.
{judge.model}, calibration tier {judge.tier}: not calibrated against human ratings.

Production cost per reply, replicating what production pays the model, recorded on most but not all trials of each arm. The extra cost per reply is a corrected contrast with an interval; the percentage uplift is arithmetic on means and carries none.
Latency, read while runs executed concurrently; input tokens, output tokens and model calls, which were not reported.
The frozen evidence of this round, run {meta.run_date}.
